correctness.rationale: All 65,536 vertex subsets and all 384 cube automorphisms are covered by the included standalone verifier. The exact augmented boundary F2 ranks (1,15,73,135,86,42,14,2) and reduced Euler -7 force rational reduced H3 dimension seven with other groups zero. Two logically distinct finite character computations agree on every element with the closed 3+4 character. Translation Fourier inversion gives one trivial weight of multiplicity three and four distinct weight-three characters of multiplicity one; signed standard S4 and transitive permutation of four weights prove both summands absolutely irreducible. Rational finite-group transfer and exact trace averaging establish the quotient results. Code was actually executed and recorded, with complete source and output included; integral equivariant structure and larger cubes are not proved.

originality.rationale: The previously published exact four-cube computation already proves the seven-sphere wedge, and Jonsson 2008 Table 1 already gives the rank seven; both are excluded from the new claim. The full primary homotopy report explicitly does not establish a canonical equivariant decomposition, and Jonsson’s 2008 paper determines cross-cycles of periodic grids rather than homology characters. Direct checks for the complete signed-coordinate group action and the explicit two-irreducible decomposition found no implication from these sources. Other indexed hypercube symmetry computations use distinct Čech or cut complexes. This supports best-knowledge originality of the 384-element rational representation, not priority certainty.

value.rationale: The full hyperoctahedral action on the standard four-cube independence complex is a natural exact topological invariant. The 3+4 split and translation weight-three spectrum distinguish symmetry behavior invisible in the already known seven-sphere homotopy type or Betti rank. In particular the translation quotient retains three rational third-cohomology directions, while the full group quotient has none and the even-permutation quotient has one. This is a meaningful finite structural calculation rather than a known-table recomputation or arbitrary parameter increment.
